name: Sharpness
whatItDoes: Increases melee damage. In Java Edition each level adds 0.5 x level + 0.5 extra damage (Sharpness V = +3); in Bedrock it adds 1.25 damage per level (Sharpness V = +6.25).
howToGet: Enchanted books from loot chests, fishing, librarian villagers and bartering
bestUses: The default damage enchantment for your main sword or axe, since it works against every mob.
keywords: sharpness enchantment sword axe damage max level

name: Protection
whatItDoes: Reduces most damage types by 4% per level per piece (up to 80% total). Covers melee, projectiles, fire, explosions and falls - everything except hunger, void and /kill damage.
howToGet: Enchanted books from loot, fishing and librarians
bestUses: Put Protection IV on all four armor pieces for general survival. Specialized protections (Fire, Blast, Projectile) only win against a single damage type.
keywords: protection enchantment armor damage reduction

name: Unbreaking
appliesTo: Tools, weapons, armor, fishing rods, bows, crossbows, tridents, shields, elytra, and more
whatItDoes: Gives each use a chance to not consume durability. For tools, III roughly quadruples lifetime; armor benefits less (about 43% longer at III).
bestUses: On every valuable item, ideally together with Mending: Unbreaking stretches durability, Mending refills it.
keywords: unbreaking enchantment durability tools armor

name: Mending
whatItDoes: XP orbs you collect repair the equipped item (2 durability per XP point) instead of filling your XP bar. Items in hand, off-hand and worn armor can be repaired.
howToGet: Treasure enchantment - NOT available from the enchanting table
Librarian villagers (any biome) selling enchanted books
Loot chests, fishing, raids (Bedrock), pillager outposts
bestUses: Your most valuable gear: netherite tools and armor, elytra, trident, bow. Combine with Unbreaking III.
keywords: mending enchantment how to get repair xp treasure

name: Efficiency
appliesTo: Pickaxes, shovels, axes, hoes and shears
whatItDoes: Increases mining speed: each level adds the square of the level plus 1 to breaking speed. Efficiency V makes stone-type blocks break almost instantly with a good pickaxe.
bestUses: Pickaxe first - mining speed defines your progress. Pair with Haste beacons for instant mining.
keywords: efficiency enchantment mining speed pickaxe

name: Fortune
whatItDoes: Multiplies drops from most ores and harvests. Fortune III averages 2.2x diamonds, up to 4x at best roll. Also increases flint, glowstone, melons and crop yields.
bestUses: A dedicated ore-mining pickaxe. Keep a separate Silk Touch pick for blocks you want unbroken.
keywords: fortune enchantment diamonds more drops

name: Silk Touch
whatItDoes: Blocks drop themselves instead of their usual items: stone instead of cobblestone, ore blocks instead of raw ore, glass, grass blocks, bee nests with bees inside, and more.
bestUses: Collecting glass, grass blocks, ore blocks for storage or decoration, moving bee nests, and mining ender chests without losing them.
keywords: silk touch enchantment blocks drop themselves

name: Looting
whatItDoes: Increases mob drops: +1 max common drop per level, and raises the chance of rare drops (wither skeleton skulls go from 2.5% to 5.5% at Looting III).
bestUses: Farming wither skeleton skulls, ender pearls, gunpowder and any mob resource. In Java, holding the sword when the mob dies is enough.
keywords: looting enchantment more drops wither skull sword

name: Feather Falling
whatItDoes: Reduces fall damage by 12% per level (48% at IV) and stacks with Protection up to the 80% cap. Also reduces ender pearl damage.
bestUses: Essential for building at height, exploring the End cities, and surviving elytra mistakes.
keywords: feather falling enchantment boots fall damage

name: Infinity
whatItDoes: You can shoot unlimited arrows as long as you carry at least one normal arrow. Tipped and spectral arrows are still consumed.
bestUses: General combat and skeleton farms where arrows are scarce. If you use tipped arrows, pick Mending instead.
keywords: infinity enchantment bow unlimited arrows

name: Fire Aspect
whatItDoes: Sets the target on fire on hit: 4 seconds per level (Fire Aspect II = 8 seconds). Burning animals drop cooked meat, and in Bedrock it also lights unlit candles, campfires and TNT when you hit them.
howToGet: Enchanted books from loot chests, fishing, librarian villagers and bartering
bestUses: Great on a mob-farm sword for auto-cooked meat. Skip it against endermen - fire makes them teleport constantly - and remember most Nether mobs are immune to fire.
keywords: fire aspect enchantment sword burn cooked meat

name: Knockback
whatItDoes: Adds about 3 blocks of knockback per level to your melee hits (Knockback II = roughly 6 extra blocks).
howToGet: Enchanted books from loot, fishing and librarian villagers
bestUses: Useful for keeping creepers at distance. Many players skip it on their main sword because it knocks mobs out of combo range and makes chaining hits harder.
keywords: knockback enchantment sword push back

name: Power
whatItDoes: Increases arrow damage by 25% x (level + 1): Power V deals 150% extra damage, up to 23 damage (11.5 hearts) on a fully drawn critical shot in Java.
howToGet: Enchanting table (levels I-IV common, V rare)
Enchanted books from loot chests, fishing, librarian villagers and bartering
Combine two Power IV bows or books in an anvil for Power V
bestUses: The number one bow enchantment. Power V one-shots most common hostile mobs with a full draw.
keywords: power enchantment bow damage max level

name: Punch
whatItDoes: Adds about 3 blocks of knockback per level to arrows (Punch II = roughly 6 extra blocks).
howToGet: Enchanted books from loot, fishing and librarian villagers
bestUses: Keeps melee mobs off you and knocks enemies off ledges; fun in PvP. Most players avoid it on endermen duty since they teleport anyway.
keywords: punch enchantment bow knockback

name: Thorns
whatItDoes: Each armor piece has a level x 15% chance to reflect 1-4 damage back to an attacker that hits you. Multiple pieces raise the chance that at least one procs, but only one piece deals damage per hit in Java.
howToGet: Enchanting table (levels I-III, rarer than most)
Enchanted books from loot, fishing and librarian villagers
bestUses: Situational: it punishes melee attackers but drains armor durability fast. Many players keep it off their main set and put it on a spare set instead.
keywords: thorns enchantment armor reflect damage durability

name: Respiration
whatItDoes: Extends underwater breathing time by 15 seconds per level (base 15s, so Respiration III = 60 seconds) and reduces how often drowning damage ticks.
howToGet: Enchanted books from loot, fishing and librarian villagers
bestUses: Essential for ocean monument raids, ruin looting and long underwater builds. Combine with Aqua Affinity and Depth Strider for the full diving set.
keywords: respiration enchantment helmet breathe underwater

name: Aqua Affinity
whatItDoes: Removes the underwater mining speed penalty - normally breaking blocks underwater takes 5x longer. With Aqua Affinity you mine at normal speed while submerged.
howToGet: Enchanted books from loot, fishing and librarian villagers
bestUses: Pair it with Respiration III for ocean monuments and underwater building. Note it does not remove the separate 5x penalty for mining while floating (not touching the floor).
keywords: aqua affinity enchantment underwater mining speed

name: Depth Strider
whatItDoes: Reduces how much water slows your movement: each level removes one third of the penalty, so Depth Strider III lets you swim at full walking speed. Also reduces how fast flowing water pushes you.
howToGet: Enchanted books from loot, fishing and librarian villagers
bestUses: Core piece of the diving set with Respiration III and Aqua Affinity for ocean monuments and underwater builds.
keywords: depth strider enchantment boots swim faster underwater

name: Soul Speed
whatItDoes: Increases movement speed on soul sand and soul soil - Soul Speed III makes you slightly faster on those blocks than normal walking on land. Each step on a soul block has a 4% chance to drain 1 boot durability.
howToGet: Barter with piglins (gold ingots) - they can offer enchanted books or iron boots with Soul Speed
Not available from the enchanting table: it is a treasure enchantment
bestUses: Soul sand valleys and nether highways. Bring spare boots or Mending - the durability drain adds up on long runs.
keywords: soul speed enchantment boots soul sand bartering treasure

name: Swift Sneak
whatItDoes: Increases sneaking speed: each level adds 15% of walking speed, so Swift Sneak III lets you sneak at 75% of normal walking speed.
howToGet: Loot chests in ancient cities in the deep dark - the only source in the game
Not available from the enchanting table, trading or fishing: it is a treasure enchantment exclusive to ancient cities
bestUses: Ancient city looting runs - sneak past sculk sensors and the Warden much faster. Apply it to leggings in an anvil.
keywords: swift sneak enchantment leggings ancient city warden sneaking faster

name: Smite
appliesTo: Swords and spears at the enchanting table; axes and maces by anvil in Java, directly in Bedrock
whatItDoes: Adds 2.5 damage per level to each hit on undead: zombies and their variants (drowned, husks, zombie villagers, zombified piglins, zoglins, zombie horses), skeletons and their variants (strays, bogged, wither skeletons, skeleton horses), phantoms and withers. In Bedrock the damage is rounded down.
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, librarian villagers, monster rooms and structure loot
bestUses: Worth it for undead-heavy trips such as the Nether fortress or a wither fight. It does nothing against other mobs, so Sharpness stays the general pick.
keywords: smite enchantment undead zombie skeleton damage max level

name: Bane of Arthropods
appliesTo: Swords and spears at the enchanting table; axes and maces by anvil in Java, directly in Bedrock
whatItDoes: Adds 2.5 damage per level against arthropods (bees, cave spiders, endermites, silverfish, spiders) and inflicts Slowness IV on them for 1 to 1.5 seconds at level I, up to 3.5 seconds at level V. In Bedrock the damage is rounded down.
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, librarian villagers and structure loot
bestUses: Useful against spider-heavy places such as mineshafts with cave spiders. It does nothing against other mobs, so most players keep Sharpness.
keywords: bane of arthropods enchantment spider silverfish slowness max level

name: Fire Protection
appliesTo: All armor pieces and turtle shell
whatItDoes: Cuts damage from fire sources by 8% per level on each piece: fire, lava, magma blocks, lit campfires, blaze projectiles, flaming arrows and burning zombies. It also shortens burning time. Blaze and magma cube contact damage and ghast fireballs are not reduced. Total damage reduction from all armor enchantments caps at 80%.
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, trial chamber vaults, librarian villagers and structure loot
bestUses: Swap it in for Protection only when one damage source is the main threat. It cannot be combined with Protection or the other protection types on the same piece.
keywords: fire protection enchantment armor lava fire damage max level

name: Blast Protection
appliesTo: All armor pieces and turtle shell
whatItDoes: Cuts damage from explosions by 8% per level on each piece (32% at level IV) and raises explosion knockback resistance by 15% per level. Covers creepers, TNT, ghast fireballs, end crystals, beds and respawn anchors, the wither, firework rockets and wind charges. Total damage reduction from all armor enchantments caps at 80%.
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, trial chamber vaults, librarian villagers and structure loot
bestUses: Swap it in for Protection only when one damage source is the main threat. It cannot be combined with Protection or the other protection types on the same piece.
keywords: blast protection enchantment creeper tnt explosion armor max level

name: Projectile Protection
appliesTo: All armor pieces and turtle shell
whatItDoes: Cuts damage from projectiles by 8% per level on each piece (32% at level IV): arrows, thrown tridents, shulker bullets, llama spit, blaze fireballs and wind charges. It also reduces direct hits from ghast fireballs and wither skulls, but not their explosions. Total damage reduction from all armor enchantments caps at 80%.
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, trial chamber vaults, librarian villagers and structure loot
bestUses: Swap it in for Protection only when one damage source is the main threat. It cannot be combined with Protection or the other protection types on the same piece.
keywords: projectile protection enchantment arrow skeleton armor max level

name: Luck of the Sea
whatItDoes: With the default loot tables it raises the chance of treasure catches by about 2.1% per level, and cuts junk by about 1.95% and fish by about 0.15% per level. At level III treasure is 11.3% of catches (5% unenchanted) and junk 4.2% (10% unenchanted).
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, librarian villagers, monster rooms and structure loot
Already on a fishing rod you catch while fishing
bestUses: Pair it with Lure on a fishing rod when you are fishing for treasure such as enchanted books and name tags.
keywords: luck of the sea enchantment fishing treasure junk max level

name: Lure
whatItDoes: Shortens the wait before something bites by 5 seconds per level. Fish cannot be caught above level V; if commands push the level beyond 5, the wait timer does not start and nothing bites.
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, librarian villagers, monster rooms and structure loot
bestUses: Level III cuts the wait by 15 seconds, which speeds up any fishing farm or treasure hunt.
keywords: lure enchantment fishing rod bite speed max level

name: Loyalty
whatItDoes: A thrown trident returns to you after it hits a block or entity. Higher levels bring it back faster: about 16.7 blocks per second at level I, 33.3 at level II and 50 at level III. If your inventory is full it circles you until a slot frees up. In Java a trident thrown into the void never returns.
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, librarian villagers, monster rooms and structure loot
bestUses: The usual choice for a trident you throw repeatedly. It cannot share a trident with Riptide.
keywords: loyalty enchantment trident return max level

name: Riptide
whatItDoes: The trident can only be thrown while you stand in water or in rain, and it launches you with it instead. Distance is (6 x level) + 3 blocks in rain or standing in water, and (4 x level) + 3 underwater. It does not work where it cannot rain unless you are in water.
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, librarian villagers, monster rooms and structure loot
bestUses: Fast travel in rainy weather or between water bodies, and a way to propel yourself with elytra in water or rain. It cannot share a trident with Loyalty or Channeling.
keywords: riptide enchantment trident launch rain water max level

name: Channeling
whatItDoes: Summons a lightning bolt when a thrown trident hits an entity or a lightning rod during a thunderstorm, including in dry biomes. It raises ranged trident damage from 8 to 13. Creepers become charged creepers, pigs become zombified piglins and villagers become witches. No opaque or partly transparent block may sit above the target.
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, librarian villagers, monster rooms and structure loot
bestUses: Used for charged creepers and as extra damage in storms. It cannot share a trident with Riptide.
keywords: channeling enchantment trident lightning thunderstorm charged creeper

name: Impaling
whatItDoes: Adds 2.5 extra damage per level on each hit, thrown or in melee. In Java only aquatic mobs take the extra damage (axolotls, dolphins, guardians, nautiluses, squid, tadpoles, turtles and fish, but not drowned). In Bedrock it applies to any mob or player touching water or rain, and the damage is rounded down.
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, librarian villagers, monster rooms and structure loot
bestUses: Best for ocean monuments and underwater hunting in Java. In Bedrock it also works on land mobs standing in rain.
keywords: impaling enchantment trident aquatic damage max level

name: Multishot
whatItDoes: A crossbow shoots two extra arrows on each shot, 10 degrees apart, but uses only one arrow. Only the central arrow can be picked up. In Java only one arrow from the same shot can damage the same mob. Tipped arrows and firework rockets are duplicated too. Each projectile costs one durability point.
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, librarian villagers, monster rooms and structure loot
bestUses: Good for groups of mobs and pairs well with Quick Charge. It cannot share a crossbow with Piercing.
keywords: multishot enchantment crossbow arrows max level

name: Piercing
whatItDoes: Arrows from the crossbow pass through as many entities as the enchantment level (level + 1 entities damaged in total) and can still be picked up. Piercing ignores shields, even when blocking, but not a closed shulker shell, the Wither armor at half health or a breeze wind armor. It has no effect on firework rockets.
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, librarian villagers, monster rooms and structure loot
bestUses: Useful against lines of mobs and against shield users. It cannot share a crossbow with Multishot.
keywords: piercing enchantment crossbow shield arrows max level

name: Quick Charge
whatItDoes: Cuts crossbow charge time by 0.25 seconds per level. The normal load time is 1.25 seconds, so Quick Charge III loads in 0.5 seconds. With commands at level V or higher in Java the crossbow loads instantly.
howToGet: Fishing, monster rooms and stronghold library chests (levels I and II)
Level III: combine two crossbows or books that both have Quick Charge II in an anvil
bestUses: A standard pick for crossbow builds, especially with Multishot or Piercing.
keywords: quick charge enchantment crossbow reload speed max level

name: Flame
whatItDoes: Arrows from a Flame bow are on fire when shot, set mobs alight and deal 5 fire damage over 5 seconds. Flaming arrows light only players, mobs, TNT, campfires and candles, not other blocks, and turn into normal arrows if fired through water or rain.
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, librarian villagers, monster rooms and structure loot
bestUses: Good against mobs that are not fire-immune.
keywords: flame enchantment bow fire arrow max level

name: Frost Walker
whatItDoes: While you walk on the ground, nearby source water becomes frosted ice within a radius of 2 + level blocks (same height, air above). The ice melts if you stop. It also removes damage from magma blocks and campfires, though not from lava.
howToGet: Treasure enchantment: not available in the enchanting table
Jungle temple and stronghold chest loot, fishing and librarian trades
bestUses: Lets you cross lakes and oceans on foot. It cannot share boots with Depth Strider.
keywords: frost walker enchantment boots water ice treasure max level

name: Curse of Binding
appliesTo: Armor, elytra, carved pumpkins, heads and turtle shells (anvil or loot)
whatItDoes: The item cannot be taken off an armor slot unless you are in Creative mode, you die or the item breaks. Items without durability and elytra only come off if you die, so removal is impossible in Hardcore. A grindstone does not remove it, and mobs are bound by it too.
howToGet: Treasure enchantment: not available in the enchanting table
Fishing, librarian trades and structure loot
bestUses: Rarely a good thing to keep. Check enchanted loot before you equip it.
keywords: curse of binding enchantment armor cannot remove treasure

name: Curse of Vanishing
appliesTo: Almost all gear with durability, plus compasses and carved pumpkins
whatItDoes: If you die with the item in your inventory it is removed from the world instead of dropping. It does not vanish if you drop it first, store it in a container, or keep inventory is on, and it does not trigger inside shulker boxes or bundles.
howToGet: Treasure enchantment: not available in the enchanting table
Fishing, librarian trades and structure loot
bestUses: Mostly a downside. A grindstone or crafting table cannot remove it, so drop the item or store it in a container before you risk dying.
keywords: curse of vanishing enchantment death item disappears treasure

name: Density
whatItDoes: Adds 0.5 damage per block fallen, per level, to a mace smash attack.
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, librarian trades and ominous vaults in trial chambers
bestUses: Built for big falls. At level V a drop of 20 blocks adds 50 extra damage. It cannot share a mace with Breach.
keywords: density enchantment mace smash attack fall damage max level

name: Breach
whatItDoes: Cuts the target's armor effectiveness by 15 percentage points per level. If armor would reduce damage by 50%, Breach I makes it 35%.
howToGet: Enchanted books from fishing, librarian trades and ominous vaults in trial chambers
bestUses: Strong against heavily armored players and mobs. It cannot share a mace with Density.
keywords: breach enchantment mace armor penetration max level

name: Wind Burst
whatItDoes: A mace smash attack launches you back into the air so you can chain smash attacks. It needs a smash attack, which means falling more than 1.5 blocks before the hit.
howToGet: Only as level I enchanted books from ominous vaults in trial chambers (about 5.5% chance per ejection)
Combine in an anvil to raise the level
bestUses: Lets you chain smash attacks, since each hit launches you back up.
keywords: wind burst enchantment mace smash attack launch ominous vault
